name: Bayesian Generator
analogy: Think of it as a trader who summarizes each chart window in a short note, but never writes a single exact value. Every note says 'about this, give or take that'. When redrawing a chart from a note, the trader picks a value within the give-or-take, so each redraw differs a little and the spread shows how unsure the trader is.

steps.title: Read the window and describe it as a range
steps.description: The encoder reads a chart window and, for each hidden feature, produces two numbers: a best value and a measure of how unsure it is. The window is described by ranges, not by single points.
steps.inExample: A window of 54 known bars, with the 6 bars after it hidden from the encoder, is described by 8 hidden features, each with a best value and a spread.

steps.title: Pick one value from inside each range
steps.description: A single value is drawn at random from within each feature's range. A trick makes this draw compatible with training, so the model can still learn from it. Different draws give different results from the same window.
steps.inExample: The first hidden feature has a best value of 4 and a spread of 3, and a draw gives 5, all counted in tenths.

steps.title: Redraw the window from the draw
steps.description: The decoder takes the drawn values and produces a full window, along with its own range of uncertainty. Because the draw varies, each redraw is slightly different.
steps.inExample: The decoder redraws all 60 bars from the 8 drawn values, with the 54 known closes within 3 points of the real ones on average.

steps.title: Keep the ranges honest with a template
steps.description: Training balances two goals: the redraw should match the real window, and the hidden ranges should stay close to a simple template, usually a bell curve centred on zero. The template keeps the hidden space tidy so that random draws from it make sense.
steps.inExample: Training pulls the best values toward zero and the spreads toward 1, so the 8 features stay close to a bell curve.

steps.title: Account for model uncertainty too
steps.description: In a Bayesian neural network variant the model's own weights are given ranges as well. Each time it runs, it draws a slightly different version of itself, so disagreement between runs shows how much the model does not know.
steps.inExample: Running the decoder 20 times with 20 draws of its hidden values gives 20 slightly different redraws of the last 6 bars.

steps.title: Generate new windows or read the uncertainty
steps.description: To generate, draw hidden values from the template and decode them. To measure uncertainty, repeat the draw many times and look at how far apart the results are.
steps.inExample: Twenty redraws of the hidden 6 bars end between 38 points below and 41 points above the last known close.

useFor.task: Generating varied synthetic windows with a measure of doubt
useFor.example: Producing 60-bar windows of 5-minute MNQ bars along with a spread that shows where the model is unsure.

useFor.task: Compressing windows into a smooth hidden space
useFor.example: Turning each window into 8 hidden values whose neighbouring values give similar windows, useful for clustering regimes.
Training with the last 6 bars of each window hidden from the encoder, then redrawing those 6 bars many times to see the width of the range of outcomes, which can inform position size.
Marking windows that the model rebuilds poorly or describes with very wide ranges as unfamiliar.

avoidWhen: You want very sharp generated samples; these models tend to produce smoother, blurrier output, and an adversarial or diffusion model gives crisper samples.
You only need a direction call; a classifier trained on that target directly, such as gradient boosting, is simpler and more accurate.

example.scenario: A researcher trained a variational generator on 60-bar windows of 5-minute MNQ bars, with the last 6 bars hidden from the encoder. For a live window of 54 known bars they ask for the hidden description, a redraw, and the spread of the 6 hidden bars across 20 draws.

input.summary: One window of 54 known bars and the settings for drawing.

fields.name: known bars
fields.meaning: How many bars the encoder reads; the 6 bars after them are what the decoder must draw.

fields.name: closing price of the last known bar
fields.meaning: The close at the end of the known bars.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical high-to-low travel of a recent bar.

fields.name: hidden features
fields.meaning: How many numbers, each with a spread, describe the window.

fields.name: draws
fields.meaning: How many times the draw and redraw are repeated for the last 6 bars.

output.summary: The hidden description, how well the known bars were redrawn, and the spread of the last 6 bars.

fields.name: first hidden feature, best value and spread
fields.meaning: The model's best value for that feature and how unsure it is.

fields.name: average error of the redrawn known closes
fields.meaning: How far the redrawn closes sit from the real closes on average.

fields.name: close after 6 more bars, middle of 20 draws
fields.meaning: The middle value of the 20 draws, about 3 points above the last known close.

fields.name: range of the 20 draws
fields.meaning: The lowest and highest outcomes in the 20 draws, showing how unsure the model is.

example.reading: The middle value is close to the last close, so the model offers no strong direction. The width of 79 points is the useful part; compare it with the average true range of 25 to see the uncertainty and check on held-out folds that the range is neither too wide nor too narrow.
